# IEEE binary16 TIFF input references

432 synthetic files generated by `../generate_tiff_half.py` using NumPy float16
and tifffile. Every input is pinned by SHA-256 in manifest.json. Samples include
negative values, signed zero, the minimum binary16 subnormal, maximum finite
65504, HDR, alpha zero/fractions/one, and hidden straight-alpha color. Cases cover
gray/RGB, gray/RGB alpha, white/black gray, associated/straight alpha, planar,
classic/BigTIFF, both byte orders, raw/Deflate, orientation and original ICC/XMP.

`../verify_tiff_half.py` independently reads binary16 samples, calculates gray
inversion and alpha division before float32 rounding, evaluates ICC curves and
matrices, checks project metadata/CRC, and compares decoded EXR/TIFF float bits.
Layer data uses float32; this adds binary16 input, not binary16 output or complete
TIFF/ICC conformance. Associated storage rounding cannot recover original
pre-multiplied color exactly; the oracle starts from actual stored samples.
